topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: These opening remarks introduce the lecture's focus on cancer evolution and outline the intended learning outcomes.

topics.label: Genetic and epigenetic drivers of clonal evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how pre-malignant tissues acquire competitive growth advantages through Darwinian clonal succession and epigenetic alterations.

topics.label: Cell of origin and cancer stem cell hierarchy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the cancer stem cell hypothesis and tissue hierarchy as determinants of tumor initiation across hematologic and intestinal models.

topics.label: Microenvironmental and inflammatory promotion of tumor growth
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how external exposures, chronic inflammation, and stromal interactions create permissive conditions that stimulate tumorigenesis and maintain established malignancies.

topics.label: Methods for studying tumor evolution and spatial architecture
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic surveys the sequencing, mathematical modeling, and spatial profiling technologies used to investigate tumor clones and their tissue environments.

topics.label: Integrative evolutionary model of cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic synthesizes the collective contribution of mutational events, cell of origin, epigenetic states, and microenvironmental pressures in shaping malignant evolution.

topics.label: Lecture closing
topics.groupedBecause: These closing remarks conclude the session and preview the upcoming lecture on cancer therapy.
